days.description: The number of days to look back for triangulation runs.

end_date.description: The end date for the data retrieval period, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. If null, defaults to the current date.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the request.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to a certificate file to verify the peer.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary mapping protocol names to URLs of the proxies.

stream.description: If true, the response should be streamed; otherwise, the response will be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not.

message.content:
Triangulation metrics are a set of quantitative measures used to evaluate the quality, reliability, and performance of triangulation processes—typically in the context of spatial data analysis, geospatial modeling, or sensor fusion. They help determine how well a triangulation algorithm or system is performing and whether the resulting triangulated mesh or point cloud meets the desired accuracy and precision requirements.

Key aspects of triangulation metrics include:

| Metric | What it Measures | Typical Use |
|--------|------------------|-------------|
| **Accuracy** | Difference between triangulated points and ground‑truth reference points. | Validating the fidelity of the triangulation against known benchmarks. |
| **Precision** | Variability of repeated triangulations under identical conditions. | Assessing consistency and repeatability of the process. |
| **Resolution** | Smallest distinguishable feature size that can be captured. | Determining the level of detail achievable. |
| **Coverage** | Proportion of the target area or volume that has been triangulated. | Ensuring complete spatial representation. |
| **Error Distribution** | Spatial pattern of errors across the triangulated domain. | Identifying systematic biases or localized issues. |
| **Computational Efficiency** | Time and resources required to generate the triangulation. | Optimizing performance for large datasets or real‑time applications. |
| **Robustness** | Ability to handle noisy or incomplete data without failure. | Evaluating resilience to data imperfections. |
| **Topology Preservation** | Maintenance of connectivity and adjacency relationships. | Ensuring structural integrity of the mesh. |
| **Scalability** | Performance as dataset size increases. | Planning for future data growth. |

These metrics are often computed using statistical tools, error analysis, and visual inspection. They guide decisions on algorithm selection, parameter tuning, and quality control in projects ranging from 3D reconstruction and GIS mapping to robotics and autonomous navigation.
